reviewScope: All 36 supplied source units, both en and literal fields, checked against Chinese and the complete linked critical passage. Each affected field is listed separately; no source files or Chinese text were changed. These are translation corrections, not date-schema amendments or publication approval.

corrections.before: The ruler exists for his people; the people live on grain.
corrections.after: The ruler takes the people as the foundation of the state; the people depend on grain for their lives.
corrections.sourceReason: 君以黎元為國 states the ruler’s dependence on the people as the state’s basis, not the different proposition that the ruler exists for the people.

corrections.before: Cap tradesmen and aides to fixed quotas; everyone else goes back to the plow.
corrections.after: The Four Assistants and the generals shall promptly fix quotas for artisans and merchants; the rest shall return to farming.
corrections.sourceReason: 百工商賈數 is the matter to be regulated; 四佐與列將 are officials instructed to fix the quotas, not aides whose numbers are being capped.

corrections.before: Hundred crafts and merchants’ numbers, four assistants and column generals quickly fix great quotas; the rest return to farming.
corrections.after: As for the numbers of artisans and merchants, let the Four Assistants and the generals promptly establish the overall quotas; let the remainder return to farming.
corrections.sourceReason: The current literal field obscures the subject and imperative. 四佐與列將速定大員 assigns the quota-setting duty to the Four Assistants and generals.

corrections.before: Strike idle students from the rolls.
corrections.after: Students unable to benefit from instruction shall also be removed from the rolls.
corrections.sourceReason: 不任訓教 concerns inability to receive or bear instruction; the adjective idle substitutes a judgment of diligence not stated here.

corrections.before: Students who do not bear training and teaching, also remove from rolls.
corrections.after: Students who are not capable of receiving instruction shall also be removed from the rolls.
corrections.sourceReason: 不任訓教 does not mean students fail to bear the work of training and teaching others. The students are recipients of instruction.

corrections.before: Feng Sheng staunchly upright, deeply attained the body of a royal minister.
corrections.after: Master Feng is steadfastly upright and deeply embodies the character of a royal minister.
corrections.sourceReason: 封生 is an honorific designation of Feng, identified earlier in the complete linked passage as 封裕, not a personal name Feng Sheng. 王臣之體 concerns ministerial character, not a physical body.

corrections.before: A black dragon and a white dragon appeared on Long Mountain; Huang led his court within two hundred paces and offered the great sacrifice.
corrections.after: A black dragon and a white dragon appeared on Long Mountain; Huang personally led his officials to observe them from more than two hundred paces away and offered a tailao sacrifice.
corrections.sourceReason: 去龍二百餘步 means more than two hundred paces away, not within two hundred. The complete primary passage reads 祭以太牢, whereas the supplied Chinese field has the anomalous 祭乙太宰; this English correction does not silently amend that Chinese field.

corrections.before: At the time there were black dragon and white dragon each one, appeared at Long Mountain; Huang personally led the group of officials to observe them, two hundred-odd steps from the dragons, sacrificed with the grand boar offering.
corrections.after: At the time, one black dragon and one white dragon appeared on Long Mountain. Huang personally led the assembled officials to observe them from more than two hundred paces away and sacrificed with a tailao offering.
corrections.sourceReason: The linked complete text has 祭以太牢, also corroborated in Tongjian’s 345 dragon notice. 太牢 is not a grand boar offering. The supplied Chinese 祭乙太宰 is a separate textual discrepancy and is not changed here.

corrections.before: He labeled elite students “high-gate pupils,” reopened the eastern school for archery rites, and each month examined their progress.
corrections.after: He gave the sons and younger brothers of his senior ministers who were official students the title “high-gate students,” established the eastern school in the old palace for the village archery rites, and personally observed and assessed their performance each month.
corrections.sourceReason: 立東庠于舊宮 establishes a school in the old palace; it does not say reopened. The fuller wording also preserves the official-student qualification and the kinship group receiving the title.

corrections.before: Because of long drought, begged off common people’s field rent.
corrections.after: Because of the prolonged drought, he remitted the common people’s field tax.
corrections.sourceReason: 丐百姓田租 in this governmental context grants remission of field tax; begged off misstates the ruler’s action and its recipient. The en field already represents remission and needs no corresponding change.

corrections.before: He abolished several empty commanderies such as Chengzhou, Jiyang, and Yingqiu.
corrections.after: He abolished Chengzhou, Jiyang, Yingqiu, and other commanderies.
corrections.sourceReason: 罷成周、冀陽、營丘等郡 does not describe the commanderies as empty. Remove that unsupported characterization; the literal field already preserves the unqualified abolition.

corrections.before: They carried him home; he briefed Murong Jun on the succession.
corrections.after: He was carried back to the palace in a litter and summoned Jun to entrust him with affairs after his death.
corrections.sourceReason: 引俊屬以後事 describes summoning Jun and entrusting him with subsequent affairs, not merely briefing him on succession; 宮 is the palace, and 輦 specifies litter conveyance.

corrections.before: Carried on litter returned palace, led Jun to entrust later affairs.
corrections.after: He returned to the palace in a litter and summoned Jun, entrusting him with affairs after his death.
corrections.sourceReason: 引俊 here summons Jun; 屬以後事 entrusts him with the affairs to follow the dying ruler, as the next sentence confirms. Led Jun to entrust later affairs obscures who entrusts whom.

corrections.before: After Murong Jun took the throne he posthumously styled his father Emperor Wenming.
corrections.after: When Murong Jun assumed the imperial title in usurpation, he posthumously honored his father as Emperor Wenming.
corrections.sourceReason: 俊僭號 means Jun’s assumption of an imperial title, not his earlier succession to the throne. Preserve 僭 and avoid conflating the later imperial claim with succession after Huang’s death. The literal field already distinguishes this action.
